note.explanation: Liquid pressure is caused by the weight of the liquid above a point. It depends on the liquid's density and the depth of the point. Pressure pushes at right angles to a surface.
examples: At the same depth, a denser liquid produces more pressure.
The lowest hole in a water-filled container has the greatest pressure.
note.simple: The deeper you go in a liquid, the more liquid is above you, so the pressure is greater.
note.checkQuestion: What happens to liquid pressure as depth increases?
note.title: Pressure in liquids
steps: Find the depth h below the liquid surface.
Use the liquid density ρ and gravitational acceleration g.
Substitute in P = ρgh, using SI units.
Give pressure in pascals (Pa), or N m⁻².

mcqs.stem: According to P = ρgh, which property of the liquid affects its pressure at a given depth?
rationales: Colour does not appear in the liquid-pressure equation.

options: At right angle to the surface
Along the edge of the surface
In the direction of gravity only
mcqs.stem: In which direction does pressure produce force on a surface?
rationales: A force parallel to the surface does not contribute to pressure.
Pressure produces force at right angle to the surface.
A force along the edge is parallel to the surface, not normal to it.
The force direction is set by the surface normal, not always by gravity.

options: All holes have the same pressure
mcqs.stem: A container has water and three holes at different heights. At which hole is the liquid pressure greatest?
rationales: The top hole is at the smallest depth, so its pressure is lower.
The middle hole is deeper than the top one but not the deepest.
The lowest hole is at the greatest depth, where liquid pressure is highest.
Pressure is not the same at different depths.

mcqs.stem: Which is the SI unit of pressure?
rationales: N m⁻² is the unit of pressure and is also called the pascal.
kg m⁻³ is a unit of density.
m s⁻² is a unit of acceleration.
kg m⁻² is not the SI unit of pressure.

written.text: Q6.4. How does water pressure one metre below the surface of a swimming pool compare to water pressure one metre below the surface of a very large and deep lake?
written.finalAnswer: The water pressures are equal because the water is at the same depth.

rubric.why: The comparison must identify that the pressures are the same.
The reason follows from pressure depending on depth and liquid density.
rubric.how: Both points are at the same depth in water, so P = ρgh gives the same pressure.

modelAnswer: The liquid is water in both cases and the depth is 1 m.
Therefore, the water pressures are equal.

written.text: Q6.5. What will happen to the pressure in all parts of a confined liquid if pressure is increased in one part? Give an example from your daily life where such principle is applied.
written.finalAnswer: The increased pressure is transmitted equally throughout the liquid; this principle is applied in hydraulic brakes.

rubric.why: The answer must describe what happens throughout the confined liquid.
rubric.description: State how the pressure change is transmitted.
rubric.how: Explain that it is transmitted equally throughout the liquid.

rubric.why: A relevant everyday application shows the principle in use.
rubric.how: Name hydraulic brakes or a hydraulic press.

modelAnswer: The increased pressure is transmitted equally throughout the confined liquid.
This principle is applied in the hydraulic brake system of automobiles.

If a question asks which factors affect liquid pressure, name depth and density; the equation also includes gravitational acceleration.
For force direction, say that pressure produces force at right angle to the surface.

example.question: EXAMPLE 6.2: Calculate the pressure of column of mercury 76 cm high. Density of mercury is 13.6 × 10³ kg m⁻³.

explain.title: Pressure comes from the liquid above
explain.body: Imagine a patch of area A at depth h. The liquid column above it has volume V = Ah and mass m = ρAh. Its weight acts on that patch.

explain.title: The liquid-pressure equation
explain.body: The force from the liquid column is F = mg = ρAhg. Dividing by area gives P = F/A = ρgh. The area cancels, so pressure depends on depth and density, not the patch's area.

explain.title: Greater depth means greater pressure
explain.body: Since P = ρgh, for the same liquid and gravity, increasing h increases pressure. That is why water from a lower hole spurts out with greater pressure.

explain.title: Pressure acts normally
explain.body: Pressure produces force at right angle to a surface. A force or its component that is parallel to the surface does not contribute to pressure.

explain.title: Pressure in a liquid spreads
explain.body: When a water-filled bag is squeezed, water squirts from its holes in different directions. This demonstrates that pressure is transmitted throughout the liquid.

mistakes: Using centimetres instead of converting the depth to metres before calculating.
Forgetting to include density or gravitational acceleration in P = ρgh.
Using the tank depth alone when a question asks for pressure at a lower level; include the full vertical depth to that point.
Giving pressure in a force unit such as newtons instead of Pa or N m⁻².
Saying pressure acts parallel to a surface; pressure produces force at right angle to it.
